story_type: false abort signal before a moon landing, fixed by rewriting the lander's software in two hours, 1971
hook: The lander kept signaling ABORT. The landing was two hours away.
narration: Their lunar module kept signaling abort, and the Moon landing was coming up.
February 1971. Alan Shepard and Edgar Mitchell had just undocked Apollo 14's lander, Antares.
If that abort signal came during the landing burn, Antares would abort automatically, and the landing would be off.
Mission Control had two hours, the time of one lunar orbit, to find a solution.
Flight controller Dick Thorson traced it to a loose particle in the abort button.
One loose speck in a switch can fake a signal.
Working against time at MIT, a programmer reprogrammed the lander's computer to ignore the false signal.
The new program was checked in a simulator at Cape Kennedy, then sent up to the crew.
[short pause] Less than ten miles above the surface, they swept across the landing site.
outcome: Antares landed at Fra Mauro, and Alan Shepard, America's first man in space, stepped onto the Moon.
title: Abort signal before a Moon landing
description:
Before Apollo 14's landing in February 1971, the lunar module Antares kept receiving a false abort signal from a loose particle in its abort button. A programmer at MIT rewrote the computer's instructions to ignore it within one orbit, and Alan Shepard and Edgar Mitchell landed at Fra Mauro. From the 1971 NASA film Apollo 14: Mission to Fra Mauro.
